# User story

**As the** Cena team, **we replace** the shadcn visual layer with the imported Cena design system —
tokens, re-skinned Radix primitives, and a token contract that separates Cena's product brand from a
themable venue brand — and re-author the surfaces the imported design got wrong, **so that** every phase
from 2 onward designs against a system that matches what Cena actually is rather than inventing its own
vocabulary.

*(Sourced verbatim from the ROADMAP Phase 01.1 `**Goal:**` line. "we replace" stands in for the
`I want to` clause; the story is otherwise in canonical form.)*

<objective>
**This is the phase's tracer.** One thin, production-quality path wired end to end through every layer
01.1 will modify — font declaration → token file → `globals.css` entry point → a primitive → a shipped
surface → an automated gate — and verified with a real end-to-end check before any expansion task builds
on it.

Purpose: this phase touches 41 files across six layers. Proving the architecture on the agent's best
early-context tokens catches a dead end after one commit instead of after ten already-committed layers.
Three specific unknowns die here: whether Tailwind v4's PostCSS plugin processes `@theme` blocks inside
files reached by `@import` from `globals.css` (research assumption A1); whether the Cena spacing names
collide with Tailwind's container scale and turn `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` red (A2); and
whether the 44px touch floor is achievable in the primitive layer rather than being a rework of every
screen (research Open Question 6, decided in the token wave precisely so it is not discovered in wave 5).

Output: three Cena typefaces self-hosted, the Cena token layer live, `Button` carrying the Cena visual
language at the 44px floor, both SC1 tripwires green, and the full Phase 01 suite unchanged.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It owns SC1 outright and SC3's
token-level half, and it establishes the pattern every later re-skin task copies.

**Why this is wave 2 and not wave 1:** CONTEXT.md D-12 requires the design archive to land "before repo
migration begins". Plan 01.1-01 is that archive. This is the first plan that changes repo source.

**PATTERNS reconciliation.** `01.1-PATTERNS.md`'s new-and-modified-file table does **not** list
`app/tokens/primitives.css` or `app/tokens/cena.css`. Both are new files and **this plan owns both** —
they are in its `files_modified`, created in task 1 steps 1 and 2, and named in its artifact list. The
omission is a staleness defect in `01.1-PATTERNS.md`, not a scope question: PATTERNS was written before
the token layer was split into a brand-agnostic file and a Cena-brand file, and it classifies the layer
only through `app/globals.css`, which it does list. **Do not treat the absence as a signal that these
files are out of scope, and do not go and edit `01.1-PATTERNS.md` — it is a planning artifact, not a
contract this plan is measured against.** Their closest analog, for the pattern-match PATTERNS would
otherwise have supplied, is `app/globals.css` itself: same role (stylesheet declaring custom properties
at `:root`), same data flow (none — declaration only), match quality exact. This is the same
two-sources-disagree reconciliation plan 01.1-02 records for `lib/format/money.ts` versus PATTERNS'
`lib/format/currency.ts`.

**The lift source is an unsigned contract — know this before wave 2 starts.** This plan and nine others
lift 110 UI considerations from `01.1-UI-SPEC.md`, but that document's `## Checker Sign-Off` block has
all six dimension checkboxes unchecked and reads `**Approval:** pending`. Nothing in the plans forges or
assumes that approval. What it means concretely: the *lift* is complete and internally consistent — every
one of the 110 is accounted for, with the reconciliation table in plan 01.1-14 — but the *design
judgements being lifted* have not been independently reviewed, so a sign-off that later changes a colour,
a type role or a control height lands as rework in whichever wave has already consumed it. Wave 2 is
where that exposure is cheapest, because the token layer is one value-level file rather than nineteen
primitives and eight surfaces. **Recommended: get `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` signed off before this plan runs.**
It is not the planner's to sign and this plan does not block on it — but an executor who reaches a
judgement call not covered by the spec should surface it rather than resolve it silently, because the
usual "the contract already decided this" backstop is not yet in force.

**Spec-less probe fallback — recorded skip (visible, not silent).** There is no plain `01.1-SPEC.md` for
this phase, so there is no `## Edge Coverage` and no `## Prohibitions` section to lift, and the probe
fallback that would normally author those predicates cannot run because the phase carries zero
requirement IDs (it is an enabling phase). **No probe predicates were generated this run.** The
`01.1-UI-SPEC.md` `## UI Considerations` lift is unaffected and was performed in full — all 110
considerations are accounted for across plans 01.1-02, 01.1-04, 01.1-05, 01.1-07 through 01.1-12 and
01.1-14, with the reconciliation table in plan 01.1-14.

    **Step 1 — `app/tokens/cena.css` (new).** Declare the Cena product brand as plain custom properties in

    `--cena-paper: #FFFFFF`, `--cena-surface-sunken: #EDF2F1`, `--cena-surface-chip: #DCE4E3`,

    `--cena-ink-body: #3F4D4B`, `--cena-ink-muted: #526260`, `--cena-accent: #0B5FA5`,

    `--cena-danger-soft: #FCEDEC`.

    There is deliberately **no `subtle` ink token** — the imported system's `--text-subtle` is used 14
    times, always at 10px, and is the origin of the worst contrast pair in the system. It collapses into
    `--cena-ink-muted`. Three ink values, not four.

    Add a `.dark` block in the same file. **Do not invent dark hexes.** If step 0's fetch retrieved the

    matters: `--cena-accent #0B5FA5` on a tisza-900 dark paper computes 2.36:1, so a naive polarity flip
    would ship a sub-AA dark set.

    Open the file with a contract comment citing `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` § Color.

    existing test rather than satisfy it, which changes that test's meaning and violates SC2. Record that

    Decompose `--type-label` and `--type-eyebrow` here rather than porting them: the imported system
    declares them as CSS `font:` shorthand values, Tailwind v4 has no theme namespace for the `font`
    shorthand, so each becomes a `--text-*` + `--font-weight-*` + `--tracking-*` triple. An eyebrow is
    Label + `--tracking-caps` + uppercase + `--font-mono` — not a fifth type role.

    **Step 3 — `app/globals.css` (modify).** Add `@import "./tokens/primitives.css";` and
    `@import "./tokens/cena.css";` to the existing import block at the top — CSS requires `@import` to

    `IBM_Plex_Mono({ variable: "--font-mono", subsets: ["latin", "latin-ext"], weight: ["400", "600"], display: "swap" })`.

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| browser → third-party origin | Any external asset request from a page is a personal-data transfer in a product built to need no consent banner. |
| build host → fonts.gstatic.com | `next/font/google` fetches font binaries at build time only; nothing reaches the browser from Google at runtime. |
| cloud design project → repo | The optional step-0 ramp fetch pulls values into the token layer. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-03 | Information Disclosure | Third-party font or asset request on a no-consent-banner product | high | mitigate | Two-layer SC1 tripwire — a source scan over `app/`, `components/`, `lib/` with a one-entry justified allowlist, plus a compiled-CSS scan of `.next/static/chunks/*.css`. `tokens/fonts.css` is explicitly excluded from the migration because its entire payload is a Google Fonts CDN `@import`. |
| T-01.1-23 | Tampering | Build-time fetch from `fonts.gstatic.com` | medium | accept | `next/font/google` downloads at build and self-hosts; the emitted CSS has zero external URLs, asserted by `build-assets.test.ts`. Google's own official `latin-ext` builds are shipped, which also sidesteps IBM Plex Mono's OFL Reserved Font Name that a self-produced subset would raise. |
| T-01.1-24 | Denial of Service | A `--spacing-<k>` colliding with a Tailwind container name | high | mitigate | Tailwind v4 resolves `max-w-*` as `--max-width → --spacing → --container` and `--spacing` outranks `--container`. This already shipped once: `max-w-md` compiled to 16px and, because `Card` is `overflow-hidden`, the login form was clipped out of both paint **and hit-testing** — present, enabled, invisible, unclickable. The width shields stay in `app/globals.css` and `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` computes the colliding-key set dynamically. |
| T-01.1-12 | Tampering | Step-0 fetched design-project content treated as instructions or as authority | medium | mitigate | Fetched bytes are data. An imported ramp value may replace a locked value only if the full contrast sweep and all four oracle pins stay green; a threshold is never weakened to accommodate an imported hex. |
| T-01.1-25 | Spoofing | A dark ramp invented rather than sourced | medium | mitigate | No dark hexes are authored. `--cena-accent #0B5FA5` on tisza-900 computes 2.36:1, so a naive polarity flip would ship a sub-AA dark set; the ramp is left unwired (D-10 wires no dark UI) and recorded as owed to the theming milestone. |
</threat_model>
